ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $BE\parallel AC$ through point B, intersecting $CD$ at E, as shown in the diagram:\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ACB=\angle CBE=90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\tan\angle BCD=\frac{1}{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ in $\triangle BCE$, $\frac{BE}{BC}=\frac{1}{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ $BC=3BE$,\\
$\because$ $BE\parallel AC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle DBE\sim \triangle DAC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{BE}{AC}=\frac{BD}{AD}$,\\
$\because$ $BD=AB$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{BE}{AC}=\frac{BD}{AD}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $AC=2BE$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{BC}{AC}=\frac{3BE}{2BE}=\boxed{\frac{3}{2}}$,

Because $BE\parallel AC$, $\triangle DBE\sim\triangle DAC$, hence $\frac{BE}{AC}=\frac{BD}{AD}$. Since $BD=AB$, we get $\frac{BD}{AD}=\frac{1}{2}$, so $AC=2BE$. Therefore $\frac{BC}{AC}=\frac{3BE}{2BE}=\boxed{\frac{3}{2}}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure, point A is at the upper left, point C is at the lower left, and line segment AC is approximately vertical; point B is located on the right side and on the oblique line extended from A to D, point D is further to the lower right, and CD is connected. The figure shows AB and BD are collinear, and CD connects from C to D.

Then reason: According to the auxiliary-line method, draw BE ∥ AC through point B, intersecting CD at E. Because the problem states ∠ACB=90°, AC ⟂ BC; and BE ∥ AC, therefore BE ⟂ BC, so △BCE is a right triangle. Since E is on CD, ∠BCE=∠BCD, so tan∠BCD=BE/BC=1/3, hence BC=3BE. On the other hand, BE ∥ AC, and A, B, D are collinear, C, E, D are collinear, so △DBE ∼ △DAC. From similar triangles, BE/AC=BD/AD. The problem states BD=AB, so AD=AB+BD=2BD, therefore BD/AD=1/2, so BE/AC=1/2, that is, AC=2BE. Thus BC/AC=3BE/2BE=3/2.
